questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about plant growth regulators (PGRs) are correct?

(a) PGRs are also variously described as plant growth substances, plant hormones or phytohormones.
(b) Growth promoters are involved in activities such as cell division, cell enlargement, pattern formation, tropic growth, flowering, fruiting and seed formation.
(c) Growth-inhibiting PGRs play an important role in plant responses to wounds and to stresses of biotic and abiotic origin, and in dormancy and abscission.
(d) Abscisic acid belongs to the group of plant growth promoters.
(e) Auxins, gibberellins and cytokinins belong to the group of plant growth inhibitors.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: PGRs are small, simple molecules of diverse chemical composition, also called plant growth substances, plant hormones or phytohormones. One group promotes growth (cell division, cell enlargement, pattern formation, tropic growth, flowering, fruiting, seed formation): auxins, gibberellins and cytokinins. The other group acts in responses to wounds and stresses and in growth-inhibiting activities such as dormancy and abscission: abscisic acid belongs here.
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (d) or (e), which swap the promoter and inhibitor groups.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: characteristics
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (term) with List-II (description).

List-I:
A. Meristematic phase
B. Phase of elongation
C. Phase of maturation
D. Redifferentiation

List-II:
I. Cells attain their maximal size in terms of wall thickening and protoplasmic modifications
II. Cells derived from a dedifferentiated meristem again lose the capacity to divide and mature to perform specific functions
III. Cells are rich in protoplasm, with large conspicuous nuclei and thin, primary, cellulosic walls having abundant plasmodesmatal connections
IV. Cells show increased vacuolation, cell enlargement and new cell wall deposition

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The constantly dividing cells at the root and shoot apex form the meristematic phase: rich protoplasm, large conspicuous nuclei, thin primary cellulosic walls with abundant plasmodesmata. Cells just behind it are in the phase of elongation (vacuolation, enlargement, new wall deposition). Further away lies the phase of maturation, where cells reach their maximal size in wall thickening and protoplasmic modification. Cells produced by a dedifferentiated meristem that again lose the capacity to divide are redifferentiated.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A swaps the meristematic and elongation descriptions; option B swaps elongation and maturation; option C swaps maturation and redifferentiation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', phases of growth; differentiation, dedifferentiation and redifferentiation
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Plants follow different pathways in response to the environment or to phases of life, and so form different kinds of structures; heterophylly is an example. This ability of plants is called:

solution.explanation: NCERT defines plasticity as the ability of plants to follow different pathways in response to the environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. Heterophylly (different leaf shapes in juvenile and mature plants, or in air and water) is the standard example.
steps: Different structures in response to environment/phase of life → plasticity
solution.why_others_wrong: Dedifferentiation is the regaining of the capacity to divide; apical dominance is the inhibition of lateral buds by the apical bud; senescence is ageing.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', development: plasticity
solution.final_answer: Option B: Plasticity

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which plant growth regulator acts as a general plant growth inhibitor and an inhibitor of plant metabolism?

solution.concept: Abscisic acid as a growth inhibitor
solution.explanation: NCERT states that ABA acts as a general plant growth inhibitor and an inhibitor of plant metabolism. It also inhibits seed germination and stimulates the closure of stomata.
steps: General growth inhibitor + metabolic inhibitor → abscisic acid
solution.why_others_wrong: Gibberellic acid, zeatin (a cytokinin) and IAA (an auxin) are all plant growth promoters.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: abscisic acid
solution.final_answer: Option C: Abscisic acid

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Water is not needed for the extension growth of plant cells, because cell enlargement does not depend on the turgidity of cells.
Statement II: Every plant organism has an optimum temperature range best suited for its growth, and any deviation from this range could be detrimental to its survival.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Plant cells grow in size by cell enlargement, which requires water; turgidity of cells helps in extension growth, and water also provides the medium for enzymatic activities. So Statement I is false. NCERT also notes that every plant organism has an optimum temperature range best suited for its growth and deviation from it could be detrimental, so Statement II is true.
steps: Statement I: false, turgidity helps extension growth
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', conditions for growth
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Abscisic acid helps seeds to withstand desiccation and other factors unfavourable for growth.
Reason (R): Abscisic acid breaks seed dormancy and initiates germination.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: ABA plays an important role in seed development, maturation and dormancy. By inducing dormancy, ABA helps seeds to withstand desiccation and other factors unfavourable for growth, so A is true. ABA induces dormancy and inhibits seed germination; it does not break dormancy, so R is false. (Breaking seed and bud dormancy is an effect of ethylene.)
steps: R: false, ABA induces dormancy and inhibits germination
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: abscisic acid
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (plant growth regulator) with List-II (physiological effect).

List-I:
A. Auxin
B. Gibberellin
C. Cytokinin
D. Ethylene

List-II:
I. Sprouting of potato tubers
II. Adventitious shoot formation
III. Prevents fruit and leaf drop at early stages
IV. Speeds up the malting process in the brewing industry

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Auxins prevent fruit and leaf drop at early stages (though they promote abscission of older, mature leaves and fruits). Gibberellins are used to speed up malting in brewing. Cytokinins help produce new leaves, chloroplasts, lateral shoot growth and adventitious shoots. Ethylene breaks seed and bud dormancy, including the sprouting of potato tubers.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option B swaps auxin and gibberellin; option C swaps cytokinin and ethylene; option D gives auxin the cytokinin effect.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: physiological effects
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the measurement of plant growth are correct?

(a) At the cellular level, growth is principally a consequence of an increase in the amount of protoplasm.
(b) Since an increase in protoplasm is difficult to measure directly, a quantity more or less proportional to it is generally measured.
(c) Growth is a reversible increase in the size of an organ or a cell.
(d) Growth is accompanied by anabolic and catabolic metabolic processes that occur at the expense of energy.
(e) The swelling of a piece of dry wood placed in water is an example of growth.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Growth is an irreversible permanent increase in size of an organ, its parts or a cell, and it is accompanied by metabolic (anabolic and catabolic) processes at the expense of energy. At the cellular level growth is mainly an increase in protoplasm; since this is hard to measure directly, a proportional quantity (fresh or dry weight, length, area, volume, cell number) is measured. Swelling of dead wood in water is reversible physical imbibition, not growth.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, C and D each include (c) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', growth; growth is measurable
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about primary and secondary growth are correct?

(a) The root apical and shoot apical meristems are responsible for primary growth and principally contribute to elongation of the plant along its axis.
(b) In dicotyledonous plants and gymnosperms, the lateral meristems, vascular cambium and cork cambium, appear later in life.
(c) The lateral meristems increase the girth of the organs in which they are active; this is secondary growth.
(d) The lateral meristems are responsible for the elongation of the plant along its axis.
(e) Secondary growth by vascular cambium is a common feature of monocotyledons.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the root and shoot apical meristems are responsible for primary growth and principally contribute to elongation along the axis. In dicotyledons and gymnosperms the lateral meristems, vascular cambium and cork cambium, appear later in life and increase the girth of the organs (secondary growth). Elongation is not their job, and monocots generally lack such secondary growth.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option B includes (d); option C includes (e) and leaves out (a); option D adds (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth generally is indeterminate
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A sigmoid growth curve is characteristic of a living organism growing in a natural environment, and it is typical for all cells, tissues and organs of a plant.
Statement II: With a limited nutrient supply, exponential growth cannot continue; growth slows down, leading to a stationary phase.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In geometric growth the initial growth is slow (lag phase), then rapid (log or exponential phase). With limited nutrients the growth slows down to a stationary phase, giving an S-shaped (sigmoid) curve. NCERT states that a sigmoid curve is characteristic of a living organism growing in a natural environment and is typical for all cells, tissues and organs of a plant. Both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', growth rates: geometric growth
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Plants retain the capacity for unlimited growth throughout their life.
Reason (R): Plants have meristems at certain locations in their body, whose cells have the capacity to divide and self-perpetuate.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: plant growth is unique because plants retain the capacity for unlimited growth throughout their life. This ability is due to the presence of meristems at certain locations in their body, whose cells can divide and self-perpetuate. R is exactly the cause of A.
steps: Meristems → unlimited growth, so R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth generally is indeterminate
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Development includes all the changes that an organism goes through during its life cycle, from germination of the seed to senescence.
Statement II: The act by which cells derived from the root apical and shoot apical meristems and the cambium mature to perform specific functions is termed dedifferentiation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Development is the sum of all changes an organism goes through in its life cycle, from seed germination to senescence, so Statement I is true. Cells derived from the apical meristems and the cambium differentiate and mature to perform specific functions; this act leading to maturation is differentiation, not dedifferentiation (which is the regaining of the capacity to divide). Statement II is false.
steps: Statement II: false, this is differentiation
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', differentiation, dedifferentiation and redifferentiation; development
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (plant or plant group) with List-II (feature described in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Grasses
B. Algae, bryophytes and pteridophytes
C. Wheat, paddy and mango
D. Papaya, watermelon and orchids

List-II:
I. Many ovules in the ovary
II. Wind pollination is quite common
III. A single ovule in the ovary
IV. Water is a regular mode of transport for the male gametes

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The number of ovules in an ovary may be one (wheat, paddy, mango) or many (papaya, watermelon, orchids). Wind pollination is quite common in grasses. Water is a regular mode of transport for the male gametes among the lower plant groups such as algae, bryophytes and pteridophytes, whereas pollination by water is rare in flowering plants.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A swaps the two pollination statements; option B swaps the single-ovule and many-ovule groups; option D gives grasses many ovules.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', the pistil, megasporangium (ovule); pollination: agents of pollination
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Inside the embryo sac, one male gamete moves towards the egg cell and fuses with its nucleus to form a diploid zygote. This fusion is called:

solution.explanation: One male gamete fuses with the nucleus of the egg cell, completing syngamy and giving the diploid zygote. The other male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei (triple fusion). Because both syngamy and triple fusion occur in one embryo sac, the phenomenon is called double fertilisation, an event unique to flowering plants.
solution.why_others_wrong: Triple fusion involves the two polar nuclei; apomixis is seed formation without fertilisation; emasculation is removal of anthers in artificial hybridisation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', double fertilisation
solution.final_answer: Option B: Syngamy

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a young anther, what occupies the centre of each microsporangium?

options.text: The tapetum, a layer of cells with dense cytoplasm
A group of compactly arranged homogeneous cells called the sporogenous tissue

solution.explanation: When the young anther is cut transversely, a group of compactly arranged homogeneous cells, the sporogenous tissue, occupies the centre of each microsporangium. It is surrounded by the wall layers: epidermis, endothecium, middle layers and, innermost, the tapetum. Each sporogenous cell is a potential pollen mother cell.
steps: Centre of a young microsporangium = sporogenous tissue
solution.why_others_wrong: The tapetum and endothecium are wall layers, not the centre; tetrads form later, after meiosis of the sporogenous cells.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', the stamen, microsporangium and pollen grain
solution.final_answer: Option D: A group of compactly arranged homogeneous cells called the sporogenous tissue

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a post-fertilisation event in a flowering plant?

options.text: Maturation of the ovule into a seed and of the ovary into a fruit
Formation of microspores from a pollen mother cell
Formation of megaspores from the megaspore mother cell
Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma

solution.explanation: Following double fertilisation, the development of endosperm and embryo, maturation of the ovule(s) into seed(s) and of the ovary into a fruit are collectively termed post-fertilisation events. Microsporogenesis, megasporogenesis and pollination all take place before fertilisation.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other three options (microsporogenesis, megasporogenesis and pollination) are pre-fertilisation events.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', post-fertilisation: structures and events
solution.final_answer: Option A: Maturation of the ovule into a seed and of the ovary into a fruit

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, the period for which pollen grains remain viable is highly variable and, to some extent, depends on:

options.text: The number of germ pores only
The number of ovules in the ovary

solution.explanation: NCERT: the period for which pollen grains remain viable is highly variable and to some extent depends on the prevailing temperature and humidity. In rice and wheat it is about 30 minutes; in some members of Rosaceae, Leguminosae and Solanaceae it is months.
steps: Viability depends partly on temperature and humidity
solution.why_others_wrong: Germ pore number, petal colour and ovule number are not given by NCERT as factors in pollen viability.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', the stamen, microsporangium and pollen grain
solution.final_answer: Option C: The prevailing temperature and humidity

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The cells of the endosperm are filled with reserve food materials. These reserves are used for:

options.text: The nutrition of the developing embryo

solution.explanation: The primary endosperm cell divides repeatedly to form the triploid endosperm. The endosperm cells are filled with reserve food materials and are used for the nutrition of the developing embryo.
steps: Endosperm = food for the developing embryo
solution.why_others_wrong: The seed coat comes from the integuments, male gametes from the generative cell of the pollen, and the endosperm lies inside the seed, so it plays no part in attracting pollinators.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', post-fertilisation: endosperm
solution.final_answer: Option D: The nutrition of the developing embryo

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Pollen grains represent the female gametophytes of flowering plants.
Statement II: The outer three wall layers of a microsporangium perform the function of protection and help in the dehiscence of the anther to release the pollen.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Pollen grains represent the male gametophytes; the embryo sac is the female gametophyte. So Statement I is false. Of the four wall layers of a microsporangium, the outer three (epidermis, endothecium and middle layers) protect it and help in dehiscence, while the innermost tapetum nourishes the developing pollen. Statement II is true.
steps: Statement I: false, pollen = male gametophyte
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', the stamen, microsporangium and pollen grain
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

Assertion (A): Pollen grains are well preserved as fossils.
Reason (R): The exine of pollen grains is made of sporopollenin, one of the most resistant organic materials known.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a mature two-celled pollen grain, the generative cell is:

options.text: Large, with abundant food reserve and a large irregularly shaped nucleus
Attached to the intine and divides to form the tube nucleus
Bigger than the vegetative cell and surrounded by its own exine
Small, spindle-shaped, with dense cytoplasm and a nucleus, and floats in the cytoplasm of the vegetative cell

solution.explanation: The vegetative cell is bigger, has abundant food reserve and a large irregularly shaped nucleus. The generative cell is small and floats in the cytoplasm of the vegetative cell; it is spindle-shaped with dense cytoplasm and a nucleus. It later divides to give the two male gametes.
steps: Generative cell: small, spindle-shaped, floats in vegetative cell
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A describes the vegetative cell. The generative cell forms the two male gametes, not a tube nucleus, and it has no exine of its own; it is the smaller of the two cells.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', the stamen, microsporangium and pollen grain: pollen grain
solution.final_answer: Option D: Small, spindle-shaped, with dense cytoplasm and a nucleus, and floats in the cytoplasm of the vegetative cell

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: All the events from pollen deposition on the stigma until the pollen tubes enter the ovule are together referred to as pollen-pistil interaction.
Statement II: In artificial hybridisation, emasculation is the removal of the anthers from a bisexual flower after the anthers have dehisced.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT defines pollen-pistil interaction as all the events from pollen deposition on the stigma until pollen tubes enter the ovule; Statement I is true. Emasculation is the removal of anthers from the flower bud before the anthers dehisce, using a pair of forceps. Removing them after dehiscence would allow self-pollination, so Statement II is false.
steps: Statement II: false, anthers are removed before dehiscence
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pollination: pollen-pistil interaction; artificial hybridisation
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
