questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the embryo of a monocotyledon such as a grass, the portion of the embryonal axis above the level of attachment of the scutellum is the:

solution.explanation: Monocot embryos have one cotyledon, the scutellum, on one side of the embryonal axis. The radicle and root cap at the lower end are enclosed in the coleorhiza. The portion of the axis above the level of attachment of the scutellum is the epicotyl, which has the shoot apex and a few leaf primordia enclosed in the coleoptile.
solution.why_others_wrong: The hypocotyl is below the cotyledon level, the radicle is the root tip and the coleorhiza is the sheath around the radicle and root cap.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', post-fertilisation: embryo
solution.final_answer: Option B: Epicotyl

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Plants such as Viola (common pansy), Oxalis and Commelina produce two types of flowers. Which of the following statements about these flowers are correct?

(a) Chasmogamous flowers are similar to the flowers of other species, with exposed anthers and stigma.
(b) Cleistogamous flowers do not open at all.
(c) In cleistogamous flowers, the anthers and the stigma lie close to each other.
(d) Cleistogamous flowers promote cross-pollination.
(e) Cleistogamous flowers depend on pollinators to bring pollen from other plants.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Chasmogamous flowers have exposed anthers and stigma like other flowers. Cleistogamous flowers do not open at all; their anthers and stigma lie close together, and when the anthers dehisce in the bud the pollen reaches the stigma. They are autogamous and produce assured seed set even without pollinators, so they do not promote cross-pollination.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and D include (d) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pollination: kinds of pollination
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A homozygous plant AA (female parent) is pollinated with pollen from a homozygous plant aa. Assuming normal double fertilisation, what are the genotypes of the seed coat, the embryo and the endosperm of the resulting seeds, respectively?

solution.explanation: The seed coat develops from the integuments of the ovule, which are tissues of the mother plant: AA. The zygote is egg (A) + male gamete (a): Aa. The primary endosperm nucleus is two polar nuclei (both A, from the same megaspore as the egg) + one male gamete (a): AAa.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A treats the seed coat as hybrid tissue and the endosperm as two paternal sets; option B gives the endosperm two paternal sets; option C swaps the seed coat and embryo genotypes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', double fertilisation; post-fertilisation: seed
solution.final_answer: Option D: AA, Aa and AAa

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In seeds of black pepper and beet, a persistent remnant of the nucellus, the perisperm, is present. Which pair of structures has the same ploidy?

solution.concept: Ploidy of seed and fruit tissues
solution.explanation: The nucellus is diploid tissue of the parent sporophyte, so the perisperm is 2n. The pericarp develops from the ovary wall, also 2n tissue of the mother plant. The endosperm is triploid (3n), the zygote is diploid (2n) and the egg cell is haploid (n).
solution.why_others_wrong: Perisperm (2n) differs from endosperm (3n); endosperm (3n) differs from the zygote (2n); the pericarp (2n) differs from the haploid egg.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', post-fertilisation: seed; fruit
solution.final_answer: Option B: Perisperm and pericarp

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A fruit contains 40 seeds. Each seed has developed from a separate ovule by normal double fertilisation, with one pollen tube entering each ovule. How many male gametes take part, and how many nuclei (male and female together) fuse in all?

solution.explanation: In each embryo sac, one pollen tube releases two male gametes. Syngamy fuses one male gamete with the egg nucleus (2 nuclei); triple fusion fuses the other male gamete with the two polar nuclei (3 nuclei). So each ovule uses 2 male gametes and 5 nuclei fuse. For 40 seeds: 2 × 40 = 80 male gametes and 5 × 40 = 200 nuclei.
solution.shortcut: Double fertilisation = 2 male gametes and 5 fusing nuclei per seed.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A counts one male gamete and only the three nuclei of triple fusion per seed; option B counts only one polar nucleus in triple fusion (4 per seed); option D counts one male gamete per seed.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', double fertilisation
solution.final_answer: Option C: 80 male gametes; 200 nuclei

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about seeds and fruits are correct?

(a) A seed is often described as a fertilised ovule, and seeds are formed inside fruits.
(b) A seed typically consists of seed coat(s), cotyledon(s) and an embryo axis.
(c) The cotyledons are generally thick and swollen due to the storage of food reserves, as in legumes.
(d) In most plants, the other floral parts persist and enlarge along with the ovary as the fruit develops.
(e) The seed is the final product of asexual reproduction in angiosperms.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the seed is the final product of sexual reproduction in angiosperms and is often described as a fertilised ovule; seeds form inside fruits. A seed has seed coat(s), cotyledon(s) and an embryo axis, and the cotyledons are generally thick and swollen with food reserves (legumes). In most plants, by the time the fruit develops from the ovary, the other floral parts degenerate and fall off.
steps: (d): false, other floral parts degenerate and fall off
(e): false, seeds result from sexual reproduction
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and C include (d) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', post-fertilisation: seed; fruit
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In artificial hybridisation, emasculated flowers are covered with a bag of suitable size, generally made up of butter paper, to prevent contamination of the stigma with unwanted pollen.
Statement II: When the stigma of the bagged flower attains receptivity, mature pollen grains collected from the anthers of the male parent are dusted on it, and the flowers are rebagged and the fruits allowed to develop.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Both statements follow NCERT's account of artificial hybridisation: after emasculation, the flowers are covered with a bag, generally of butter paper (bagging). When the stigma becomes receptive, pollen from the desired male parent is dusted on it, and the flowers are rebagged so that fruits develop only from the intended cross.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pollination: artificial hybridisation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A plant species with bisexual flowers is self-incompatible. Which kind of pollination can lead to seed set by fertilisation in this species?

options.text: Both autogamy and geitonogamy, but not xenogamy

solution.explanation: Self-incompatibility is a genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen, from the same flower or from other flowers of the same plant, from fertilising the ovules, by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the pistil. Autogamy (same flower) and geitonogamy (another flower of the same plant) both bring self-pollen. Only xenogamy, which brings pollen from a different plant, can lead to fertilisation.
steps: Self-pollen = same flower + other flowers of same plant
solution.why_others_wrong: Autogamy and geitonogamy both deliver self-pollen, which self-incompatibility rejects; geitonogamy is genetically similar to autogamy.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', outbreeding devices
solution.final_answer: Option A: Xenogamy only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (character studied by Mendel in pea) with List-II (recessive trait).

List-I:
A. Flower colour
B. Seed shape
C. Stem height
D. Flower position

List-II:
I. Terminal
II. Dwarf
III. White
IV. Wrinkled

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Mendel studied seven pairs of contrasting traits. For these four characters the dominant and recessive traits are: flower colour violet/white, seed shape round/wrinkled, stem height tall/dwarf, flower position axial/terminal. The recessive forms are white, wrinkled, dwarf and terminal.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A swaps flower colour and seed shape; option C swaps stem height and flower position; option D swaps flower colour and stem height.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', Mendel's laws of inheritance
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a Mendelian disorder, i.e. one determined by alteration or mutation in a single gene?

solution.explanation: NCERT lists the most common Mendelian disorders as haemophilia, cystic fibrosis, sickle-cell anaemia, colour blindness, phenylketonuria and thalassemia. Down's, Klinefelter's and Turner's syndromes are chromosomal disorders caused by an extra or missing chromosome.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other three are chromosomal disorders (trisomy 21, 47 XXY and 45 X0).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: Mendelian disorders
solution.final_answer: Option D: Cystic fibrosis

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In genetics, 'variation' is best defined as:

options.text: The degree by which progeny differ from their parents
The process by which characters are passed on from parent to progeny
The complete expression of a dominant allele in the heterozygote
The physical association of two genes on a chromosome

solution.explanation: Genetics deals with inheritance as well as variation of characters. Inheritance is the process by which characters are passed on from parent to progeny; it is the basis of heredity. Variation is the degree by which progeny differ from their parents.
steps: Variation = degree of difference between progeny and parents
solution.why_others_wrong: Option B defines inheritance, option C describes dominance and option D describes linkage.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', introduction
solution.final_answer: Option A: The degree by which progeny differ from their parents

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the haplodiploid sex-determination system of honey bees, the male (drone) produces sperms by:

options.text: Meiosis, which halves its 32 chromosomes to 16
Meiosis, because the male is diploid
Mitosis, because the male is haploid

solution.explanation: In honey bees, a fertilised egg develops into a female (queen or worker) with 32 chromosomes, and an unfertilised egg develops into a haploid male (drone) with 16 chromosomes by parthenogenesis. NCERT notes as a special feature that the males produce sperms by mitosis.
steps: Haploid cell cannot undergo normal meiosis → sperms by mitosis
solution.why_others_wrong: The male has only 16 chromosomes and is haploid, so it does not halve 32 chromosomes by meiosis. Parthenogenesis is how the male itself develops, not how it makes sperms.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex determination: sex determination in honey bee
solution.final_answer: Option C: Mitosis, because the male is haploid

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In haemophilia, why does a simple cut in an affected individual result in non-stop bleeding?

options.text: The red blood cells become sickle-shaped under low oxygen tension
A single protein that is part of the cascade of proteins involved in blood clotting is affected
Too few globin molecules are synthesised
The enzyme phenylalanine hydroxylase is absent

solution.explanation: Haemophilia is a sex-linked recessive disease. In it, a single protein that is a part of the cascade of proteins involved in the clotting of blood is affected, so a simple cut results in non-stop bleeding.
steps: Haemophilia → defect in one clotting-cascade protein
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A describes sickle-cell anaemia, option C thalassemia and option D phenylketonuria.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: haemophilia
solution.final_answer: Option B: A single protein that is part of the cascade of proteins involved in blood clotting is affected

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a polygenic trait, the phenotype reflects the contribution of each allele. The effect of each allele is therefore described as:

options.text: Epistatic and masked by one dominant allele

solution.explanation: Polygenic traits are controlled by three or more genes. NCERT notes that in a polygenic trait the phenotype reflects the contribution of each allele, i.e. the effect of each allele is additive, which is why skin colour shows a gradation of shades.
steps: Each allele adds its share → additive effect
solution.why_others_wrong: Polygenic alleles are not masked by a single dominant allele, are not lethal and are not sex-limited.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', polygenic inheritance
solution.final_answer: Option D: Additive

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In humans, the male is heterogametic. In what proportion does he produce sperms carrying the X and the Y chromosome?

options.text: 50 per cent X-bearing and 50 per cent Y-bearing
75 per cent X-bearing and 25 per cent Y-bearing

solution.explanation: Human males have XY sex chromosomes and produce two types of gametes: 50 per cent of the sperms carry the X chromosome and 50 per cent carry the Y. Females (XX) produce only X-bearing ova, so the sex of the child is decided by the type of sperm that fertilises the ovum.
steps: XY male → X and Y sperms in 1 : 1
solution.why_others_wrong: An XY cell gives X and Y to its products equally at meiosis, so neither all-X, all-Y nor 3 : 1 is possible.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex determination: sex determination in humans
solution.final_answer: Option C: 50 per cent X-bearing and 50 per cent Y-bearing

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A plant heterozygous for three independently assorting genes (AaBbCc), each with complete dominance, is self-pollinated. How many different phenotypes and how many different genotypes are expected in the progeny?

solution.concept: Phenotype and genotype classes in a trihybrid cross
solution.explanation: For each gene, Aa × Aa gives 2 phenotypes (dominant, recessive) and 3 genotypes (AA, Aa, aa). With independent assortment the classes multiply: phenotypes 2³ = 8, genotypes 3³ = 27.
solution.shortcut: n heterozygous genes selfed: 2ⁿ phenotypes, 3ⁿ genotypes, 4ⁿ gamete combinations.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option B multiplies 2 × 3 instead of raising to the power of three; option C gives 4³ = 64, the number of gamete combinations (boxes in the Punnett square), not distinct genotypes; option D swaps the two numbers.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of two genes; law of independent assortment
solution.final_answer: Option A: 8 phenotypes and 27 genotypes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: One reason Mendel's work remained unrecognised was that he could not provide any physical proof for the existence of factors or say what they were made of.
Statement II: By 1900, advances in microscopy allowed scientists to observe cell division carefully, which led to the discovery of nuclear structures that appeared to double and divide just before each cell division.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Rediscovery of Mendel and the chromosomal theory
solution.explanation: NCERT gives several reasons why Mendel's work stayed unrecognised; one is that he could not provide any physical proof for the existence of factors or say what they were made of. By 1900 advances in microscopy allowed careful observation of cell division and led to the discovery of structures in the nucleus that doubled and divided before each division: the chromosomes ('coloured bodies', as they were seen after staining). Both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', chromosomal theory of inheritance
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Dominance is not an autonomous feature of a gene or of the product that it has information for.
Reason (R): Dominance depends on the gene product and the production of a particular phenotype from it, as well as on the particular phenotype that we choose to examine when more than one phenotype is influenced by the same gene.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: dominance is not an autonomous feature of a gene or its product. It depends as much on the gene product and the production of a particular phenotype from this product as on the phenotype we choose to examine (as in the pea gene for starch synthesis, which is dominant for seed shape but incompletely dominant for starch grain size). R explains why A is true.
steps: Dominance depends on the product and the phenotype examined → not autonomous
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: concept of dominance
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (cross between parents of given ABO genotypes) with List-II (blood groups possible among the children).

List-I:
A. IᴬIᴬ × ii
B. IᴬIᴮ × ii
C. Iᴬi × ii
D. IᴬIᴬ × IᴮIᴮ

List-II:
I. Blood groups A and O only
II. Blood group AB only
III. Blood group A only
IV. Blood groups A and B only

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Multiple alleles and co-dominance in the ABO system
solution.explanation: The gene I has three alleles, Iᴬ, Iᴮ and i; Iᴬ and Iᴮ are co-dominant and both are dominant over i. IᴬIᴬ × ii gives only Iᴬi (A). IᴬIᴮ × ii gives Iᴬi (A) and Iᴮi (B). Iᴬi × ii gives Iᴬi (A) and ii (O). IᴬIᴬ × IᴮIᴮ gives only IᴬIᴮ (AB).
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A swaps the crosses IᴬIᴬ × ii and Iᴬi × ii; option B treats IᴬIᴮ × ii as giving AB children; option D gives the IᴬIᴮ × ii parents children of groups A and O.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: co-dominance (ABO blood groups)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the chromosomal theory of inheritance and Morgan's work are correct?

(a) Sutton and Boveri argued that the pairing and separation of a pair of chromosomes would lead to the segregation of the pair of factors they carried.
(b) Morgan crossed yellow-bodied, white-eyed female Drosophila with brown-bodied, red-eyed males and intercrossed their F1 progeny.
(c) Genes that are very tightly linked show a high frequency of recombination.
(d) Genes that are loosely linked show a higher recombination than tightly linked genes.
(e) Chromosomes and genes both segregate at gamete formation such that only one of each pair is transmitted to a gamete.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Sutton and Boveri linked the pairing and separation of chromosomes to the segregation of Mendel's factors; genes and chromosomes both occur in pairs and both segregate so that only one of each pair goes to a gamete. Morgan crossed yellow-bodied, white-eyed females with brown-bodied, red-eyed males and intercrossed the F1. He found that some genes were very tightly linked (very low recombination) while others were loosely linked (higher recombination).
steps: (c): false, tight linkage means low recombination
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option contains (c), which reverses the relation between linkage and recombination.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', chromosomal theory of inheritance; linkage and recombination
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (d) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
A haemophilic man marries a woman who is neither haemophilic nor a carrier. Which of the following statements about their children are correct?

(a) All their sons will be normal.
(b) All their daughters will be carriers.
(c) Half of their sons will be haemophilic.
(d) Half of their daughters will be haemophilic.
(e) A son can inherit the defective allele from his father.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Haemophilia is X-linked recessive. The father is XʰY and the mother XᴴXᴴ. Sons receive the Y from the father and an Xᴴ from the mother, so all sons are normal. Daughters receive Xʰ from the father and Xᴴ from the mother, so all daughters are unaffected carriers. A father never passes his X chromosome to a son.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A includes (e), but sons get the father's Y, not his X. Options B and C include (c) or (d), which would need a carrier mother.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: haemophilia
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a) and (b) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Suppose a polygenic trait is controlled by three genes A, B and C, and each dominant allele adds an equal amount to the phenotype (additive effect). In the progeny of AaBbCc × AaBbCc, how many distinct phenotypic classes are expected?

solution.concept: Number of phenotypic classes in polygenic inheritance
solution.explanation: With additive alleles, the phenotype depends only on the number of dominant alleles an individual carries. Offspring of AaBbCc × AaBbCc can carry 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 dominant alleles, giving 7 distinct classes (from the lightest, aabbcc, to the darkest, AABBCC).
solution.why_others_wrong: 8 is the number of phenotypes if each gene showed complete dominance; 27 is the number of genotypes; 6 leaves out the class with no dominant allele (aabbcc).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', polygenic inheritance
solution.final_answer: Option B: 7

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Chromosomal disorders are caused by the absence or excess or abnormal arrangement of one or more chromosomes.
Statement II: Individuals with Klinefelter's syndrome are sterile females with rudimentary ovaries.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: chromosomal disorders are caused by absence or excess or abnormal arrangement of one or more chromosomes, so Statement I is true. Klinefelter's syndrome (47, XXY) individuals show overall masculine development with some feminine development (gynaecomastia) and are sterile males. Sterile females with rudimentary ovaries describe Turner's syndrome. Statement II is false.
steps: Statement II: false, describes Turner's syndrome
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: chromosomal disorders
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the F2 generation of Mendel's dihybrid cross between round yellow and wrinkled green pea plants, only the parental combinations of traits appeared.
Reason (R): During gamete formation, the segregation of one pair of alleles is independent of the other pair.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Recombinant phenotypes in a dihybrid cross
solution.explanation: R is the law of independent assortment and is true. Because the two pairs assort independently, the F2 showed the new combinations round green and wrinkled yellow as well as the parental types, in the ratio 9 : 3 : 3 : 1. A is false.
steps: A: false, round green and wrinkled yellow also appeared
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of two genes
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In Mendel's dihybrid cross RRYY × rryy, the F1 plants (RrYy) are self-pollinated. If one F2 seed is picked at random from among the round yellow seeds only, what is the probability that it is true-breeding (RRYY)?

solution.concept: Conditional probability in the dihybrid F2
solution.explanation: Round yellow seeds make up 9 of the 16 F2 combinations: 1 RRYY, 2 RRYy, 2 RrYY and 4 RrYy. Only RRYY breeds true for both traits. Given that the seed is round yellow, the probability is 1/9.
solution.shortcut: Within the 9 class: genotypes are 1 : 2 : 2 : 4 (RRYY : RRYy : RrYY : RrYy).
solution.why_others_wrong: 1/16 is the fraction of RRYY among all F2 seeds, ignoring the condition; 4/9 is the chance of RrYy; 9/16 is the fraction of round yellow seeds itself.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of two genes
solution.final_answer: Option D: 1/9

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
A woman who is a carrier for haemophilia marries a normal man. Which of the following statements about their children are correct?

(a) Half of their sons are expected to be haemophilic.
(b) One-fourth of all their children are expected to be haemophilic sons.
(c) None of their daughters is expected to be haemophilic.
(d) Half of their daughters are expected to be carriers.
(e) Half of all their children are expected to be haemophilic.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Mother XᴴXʰ × father XᴴY gives four equally likely children: XᴴXᴴ (normal daughter), XᴴXʰ (carrier daughter), XᴴY (normal son) and XʰY (haemophilic son). So 1/2 of the sons and 1/4 of all children are haemophilic; no daughter is haemophilic (each gets the father's Xᴴ); 1/2 of the daughters are carriers.
steps: Affected: XʰY only = 1/2 of sons = 1/4 of all
solution.why_others_wrong: Options B, C and D include (e), which confuses 'half of the sons' with 'half of all the children'.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: haemophilia
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A colour-blind man cannot pass the gene for colour blindness on to his son.
Reason (R): A son receives his X chromosome from his mother and his Y chromosome from his father.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: No father-to-son transmission of X-linked genes
solution.explanation: The gene for red-green colour blindness is on the X chromosome. A son gets the Y chromosome from his father and the X from his mother, so a colour-blind father can never transmit the gene to his sons (he passes it to all his daughters). R correctly explains A.
steps: Father's X goes only to daughters → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex-linked inheritance; genetic disorders: colour blindness
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In snapdragon, the F2 genotypic ratio for flower colour differs from that of a Mendelian monohybrid cross.
Statement II: A cross between a pink-flowered and a white-flowered snapdragon gives pink and white offspring in a 1 : 1 ratio, with no red-flowered offspring.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In snapdragon (RR red, Rr pink, rr white), the F2 genotypes are 1 RR : 2 Rr : 1 rr, exactly as in a Mendelian monohybrid cross; only the phenotypic ratio changes from 3 : 1 to 1 : 2 : 1. So Statement I is false. Pink × white is Rr × rr, giving 1 Rr (pink) : 1 rr (white) and no RR (red), so Statement II is true.
steps: Statement I: false, genotypic ratio is the usual 1 : 2 : 1
Statement II: Rr × rr → 1 pink : 1 white; true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: incomplete dominance
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Aneuploidy is the gain or loss of chromosome(s) due to failure of segregation of chromatids during cell division. Which of the following conditions result from aneuploidy?

(a) Down's syndrome
(b) Klinefelter's syndrome
(c) Turner's syndrome
(d) Sickle-cell anaemia
(e) Haemophilia

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Down's syndrome is trisomy of chromosome 21 (gain), Klinefelter's syndrome is 47, XXY (gain of an X) and Turner's syndrome is 45, X0 (loss of an X); all three are aneuploid chromosomal disorders. Sickle-cell anaemia and haemophilia are Mendelian disorders caused by alteration of a single gene; the chromosome number is normal.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A leaves out Klinefelter's syndrome, a gain of a sex chromosome; options B and D include single-gene (Mendelian) disorders.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: chromosomal disorders
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Two genes are so tightly linked on one chromosome that no recombination occurs between them. A dihybrid that received AB from one parent and ab from the other is test-crossed with an ab/ab plant. The progeny are expected to be:

options.text: AaBb, Aabb, aaBb and aabb in a 1 : 1 : 1 : 1 ratio
Only the two parental types, AaBb and aabb, in a 1 : 1 ratio
Mostly Aabb and aaBb, with few AaBb and aabb

solution.concept: Complete linkage in a test cross
solution.explanation: With no recombination, the dihybrid forms only the parental gametes AB and ab, in equal numbers. Crossed with ab gametes, these give AaBb and aabb in a 1 : 1 ratio. The 1 : 1 : 1 : 1 ratio is expected only for independently assorting genes, and recombinant types (Aabb, aaBb) need crossing over.
steps: No crossing over → gametes AB and ab only
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A is the result for independent assortment; option C ignores the ab gametes; option D makes the recombinants the majority, the reverse of linkage.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', linkage and recombination
solution.final_answer: Option B: Only the two parental types, AaBb and aabb, in a 1 : 1 ratio

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Both parents have blood group AB. Which of the following correctly describes their children?

options.text: All children have blood group AB
Blood groups A, B, AB and O in equal proportions
Blood groups A and B in the ratio 1 : 1; no child has blood group AB
Blood groups A, AB and B in the ratio 1 : 2 : 1; no child has blood group O

solution.concept: Co-dominance in a cross of two heterozygotes
solution.explanation: IᴬIᴮ × IᴮIᴬ gives IᴬIᴬ, IᴬIᴮ, IᴮIᴬ and IᴮIᴮ, i.e. 1 A : 2 AB : 1 B. Because Iᴬ and Iᴮ are co-dominant, the heterozygotes show group AB. Neither parent carries i, so no child can be group O. The phenotypic ratio equals the genotypic ratio, as in any co-dominant monohybrid cross.
steps: Gametes: Iᴬ, Iᴮ from each parent
IᴬIᴬ : IᴬIᴮ : IᴮIᴮ = 1 : 2 : 1 → A : AB : B
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A treats AB parents as true-breeding; option B needs both parents to carry i; option C ignores the IᴬIᴮ children.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: co-dominance
solution.final_answer: Option D: Blood groups A, AB and B in the ratio 1 : 2 : 1; no child has blood group O

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A nucleotide is formed when a phosphate group is linked to the 5'-OH of a nucleoside. This linkage is a:

solution.explanation: A nitrogenous base linked to the pentose sugar through an N-glycosidic linkage forms a nucleoside. When a phosphate group is linked to the 5'-OH of a nucleoside through a phosphoester linkage, a nucleotide is formed. Two nucleotides are then joined to each other through a 3'–5' phosphodiester linkage.
solution.why_others_wrong: The N-glycosidic linkage joins base and sugar; the phosphodiester linkage joins two nucleotides; hydrogen bonds join bases of opposite strands.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', structure of polynucleotide chain
solution.final_answer: Option B: Phosphoester linkage

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In which of the following does RNA act as the genetic material?

options.text: Tobacco mosaic virus and QB bacteriophage

solution.explanation: DNA is the genetic material in most organisms. NCERT notes that in some viruses, such as tobacco mosaic viruses and QB bacteriophage, RNA is the genetic material.
solution.why_others_wrong: Bacteria, humans and Drosophila have DNA genomes; NCERT gives the genome sizes of bacteriophages lambda and φX174 as DNA (base pairs and nucleotides of DNA).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', properties of genetic material (DNA versus RNA)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Tobacco mosaic virus and QB bacteriophage

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (term) with List-II (description).

List-I:
A. Cistron
B. sRNA
C. Nucleoside
D. Heterochromatin

List-II:
I. A nitrogenous base linked to a pentose sugar
II. Densely packed, dark-staining and transcriptionally inactive chromatin
III. Segment of DNA coding for a polypeptide
IV. Earlier name of tRNA (soluble RNA)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: A cistron is a segment of DNA coding for a polypeptide. tRNA was called sRNA (soluble RNA) before the genetic code was postulated. A nucleoside is a nitrogenous base linked to a pentose sugar (by an N-glycosidic linkage). Chromatin that is densely packed and stains dark is heterochromatin; it is transcriptionally inactive.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option B swaps cistron and sRNA; option C swaps nucleoside and heterochromatin; option D swaps cistron and nucleoside.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', packaging of DNA helix; transcription unit and the gene; tRNA
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the Hershey–Chase experiment, bacteria were infected with bacteriophages grown on a medium containing radioactive sulphur and were then blended and centrifuged. The bacterial cells were found to be:

options.text: Radioactive, showing that the viral protein entered the bacteria
Radioactive, showing that the viral DNA contains sulphur
Not radioactive, showing that the viral protein did not enter the bacteria
Not radioactive, because the bacteria were killed before infection

solution.explanation: Viruses grown with radioactive sulphur had radioactive protein (proteins contain sulphur, DNA does not). Bacteria infected with these viruses were not radioactive after blending and centrifugation, indicating that proteins did not enter the bacteria. Bacteria infected with viruses carrying radioactive (phosphorus-labelled) DNA were radioactive. Hence DNA, not protein, passes from virus to bacterium.
steps: Bacteria not radioactive → protein did not enter
solution.why_others_wrong: The labelled protein coats were removed by blending; DNA contains phosphorus, not sulphur; the bacteria were live hosts during infection.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', the search for genetic material: Hershey–Chase experiment
solution.final_answer: Option C: Not radioactive, showing that the viral protein did not enter the bacteria

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs of nitrogenous bases are both purines?

solution.explanation: Nitrogenous bases are of two types: purines (adenine and guanine) and pyrimidines (cytosine, uracil and thymine). Cytosine is common to DNA and RNA; thymine is in DNA and uracil in RNA in place of thymine.
solution.why_others_wrong: Cytosine, thymine and uracil are all pyrimidines.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', structure of polynucleotide chain
solution.final_answer: Option A: Adenine and guanine

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Besides the lac operon, which of the following bacterial operons are named in NCERT?

options.text: trp, ara, his and val operons

solution.explanation: In bacteria, a polycistronic structural gene regulated by a common promoter and regulatory genes is called an operon. NCERT names the lac operon, trp operon, ara operon, his operon and val operon as examples.
steps: Operon examples: lac, trp, ara, his, val
solution.why_others_wrong: z, y and a are structural genes within the lac operon; σ and ρ are transcription factors of bacterial RNA polymerase; VNTRs and SNPs are DNA sequence variations, not operons.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', regulation of gene expression: the lac operon
solution.final_answer: Option D: trp, ara, his and val operons

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In prokaryotes, the predominant site for the control of gene expression is:

options.text: Control of the rate of transcriptional initiation
Transport of mRNA from the nucleus to the cytoplasm
Capping and tailing of the primary transcript

solution.concept: Regulation of gene expression in prokaryotes
solution.explanation: NCERT: in prokaryotes, control of the rate of transcriptional initiation is the predominant site for control of gene expression. The activity of RNA polymerase at a promoter is regulated by accessory proteins, and repressors acting at the operator regulate access to the promoter.
solution.why_others_wrong: Splicing, capping and tailing, and transport from a nucleus are features of eukaryotic gene expression; prokaryotes have no nucleus and their genes are not split.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', regulation of gene expression
solution.final_answer: Option B: Control of the rate of transcriptional initiation

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): During transcription, only one strand of a DNA segment is copied into RNA.
Reason (R): If both strands were copied, the two RNAs would have different sequences and could code for two different proteins, and, being complementary, they would form double-stranded RNA that could not be translated.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Why only one DNA strand is transcribed
solution.explanation: NCERT gives two reasons why both strands are not copied. Two RNAs from the two strands would have different sequences, so one DNA segment would code for two different proteins and complicate information transfer. Also, the two RNAs would be complementary and would form double-stranded RNA, preventing translation and making transcription futile. R explains A.
steps: R gives NCERT's reasons for A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', transcription
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The coding strand of a short stretch of a structural gene reads 5'-ATGCCGTTAGCA-3'. The mRNA transcribed from this stretch will be:

solution.explanation: The template strand (3'→5') is copied, so the RNA is complementary to the template and therefore has the same sequence and polarity as the coding strand, with uracil in place of thymine: 5'-AUGCCGUUAGCA-3'.
steps: mRNA = coding strand with U for T
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A is the complement of the coding strand (it would be built on the coding strand, which is not copied); option B reverses the sequence; option D keeps thymine, which RNA does not contain.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', transcription: transcription unit
solution.final_answer: Option C: 5'-AUGCCGUUAGCA-3'

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
In Griffith's experiments with Streptococcus pneumoniae, which of the following observations were made?

(a) Mice injected with live S strain bacteria died.
(b) Mice injected with live R strain bacteria lived.
(c) Mice injected with heat-killed S strain bacteria died.
(d) Mice injected with a mixture of heat-killed S strain and live R strain bacteria died.
(e) Living S strain bacteria were recovered from the mice that died after the mixed injection.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Live S strain (virulent) killed mice; live R strain did not. Heat-killed S strain did not kill mice. A mixture of heat-killed S and live R killed the mice, and living S bacteria were recovered from them: the R strain had been transformed by some 'transforming principle' from the heat-killed S strain.
steps: (c): false, heat-killed S bacteria did not kill the mice
solution.why_others_wrong: Options B, C and D include (c); heat-killed S bacteria alone are harmless.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', the search for genetic material: transforming principle
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b), (d) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: RNA cannot directly code for the synthesis of proteins; it depends on DNA to express characters.
Statement II: DNA, being double-stranded and having a complementary strand, further resists changes by evolving a process of repair.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: DNA versus RNA as genetic material
solution.explanation: NCERT: RNA can directly code for the synthesis of proteins and hence can easily express characters, whereas DNA depends on RNA for protein synthesis. Statement I reverses this and is false. DNA evolved from RNA with chemical modifications that make it more stable; being double-stranded with a complementary strand, it further resists changes by evolving a repair process. Statement II is true.
steps: Statement I: false, it is DNA that depends on RNA
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', properties of genetic material; RNA world
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (level of regulation of gene expression in eukaryotes) with List-II (event regulated).

List-I:
A. Transcriptional level
B. Processing level
C. Transport level
D. Translational level

List-II:
I. Synthesis of the polypeptide on ribosomes from mRNA
II. Formation of the primary transcript
III. Regulation of splicing
IV. Movement of mRNA from the nucleus to the cytoplasm

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Levels of regulation of gene expression
solution.explanation: In eukaryotes, regulation can be exerted at (i) the transcriptional level (formation of the primary transcript), (ii) the processing level (regulation of splicing), (iii) transport of mRNA from the nucleus to the cytoplasm and (iv) the translational level.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A swaps transcription and processing; option B swaps transport and translation; option C swaps transcription and translation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', regulation of gene expression
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Human genome project and DNA fingerprinting
questions.question_text: The haploid human genome has approximately 3 × 10⁹ bp. If the cost of sequencing was US $3 per bp (the estimated cost at the beginning of the Human Genome Project), the approximate total cost of sequencing would be:

solution.concept: Scale of the Human Genome Project
solution.explanation: Cost = number of base pairs × cost per base pair = 3 × 10⁹ × 3 = 9 × 10⁹ US dollars, i.e. about 9 billion US dollars, the figure NCERT gives to show the enormity of the project.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 billion forgets to multiply by the cost per bp; 1 billion divides instead of multiplying; 18 billion counts both copies of a diploid genome, but the estimate is for the 3 × 10⁹ bp genome.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', human genome project
solution.final_answer: Option B: 9 billion US dollars

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The split-gene arrangement probably represents an ancient feature of the genome; the presence of introns is reminiscent of antiquity, and splicing represents the dominance of the RNA world.
Statement II: Split genes are typical of bacterial genes, and introns are absent from eukaryotic genes.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT states that split-gene arrangements probably represent an ancient feature of the genome, that introns are reminiscent of antiquity and that splicing represents the dominance of the RNA world; Statement I is true. Split genes, with exons interrupted by introns, are a feature of eukaryotes; bacterial genes are not split. Statement II is false.
steps: Statement II: false, split genes are eukaryotic
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', transcription: transcription in eukaryotes
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): DNA-dependent DNA polymerases must catalyse polymerisation not only fast but also with a high degree of accuracy.
Reason (R): Errors made during DNA replication never lead to mutations.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: DNA polymerases have to polymerise a large number of nucleotides in a very short time and with high accuracy, so A is true. NCERT notes that any mistake during replication would result in mutations, so R is false.
steps: R: false, replication errors result in mutations
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication: the machinery and the enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In its inactive state, the ribosome exists as a single, undivided particle.
Statement II: The translation of an mRNA into protein begins when the small subunit of the ribosome encounters the mRNA.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The ribosome is the cellular factory for protein synthesis. In its inactive state it exists as two subunits, a large and a small one, so Statement I is false. When the small subunit encounters an mRNA, the process of translation begins. Statement II is true.
steps: Statement I: false, two separate subunits
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', translation
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Human genome project and DNA fingerprinting
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about DNA fingerprinting are correct?

(a) DNA from every tissue of an individual, such as blood, hair follicle, skin, bone, saliva or sperm, shows the same degree of polymorphism.
(b) The band pattern obtained differs from individual to individual in a population, except in monozygotic (identical) twins.
(c) The VNTR used as a probe belongs to a class of satellite DNA referred to as mini-satellite.
(d) The use of PCR has reduced the sensitivity of the technique, so large amounts of tissue are now needed.
(e) DNA fingerprinting is based on differences in the protein-coding sequences, which make up most of the human genome.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: DNA from any tissue of an individual shows the same polymorphism, which is why blood, hair follicles, saliva or sperm can be used. The VNTR probe is a mini-satellite; VNTR sizes vary, giving bands that differ between individuals except monozygotic twins. PCR has increased the sensitivity, so DNA from a single cell is enough. Fingerprinting uses repetitive (satellite) DNA, and less than 2 per cent of the genome codes for proteins.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and D include (d) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', DNA fingerprinting
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: E. coli grown for many generations in a ¹⁵NH₄Cl medium is transferred to a ¹⁴NH₄Cl medium. E. coli divides once every 20 minutes and DNA replicates semiconservatively. After 80 minutes, what fractions of the DNA molecules are hybrid (¹⁵N/¹⁴N) and light (¹⁴N/¹⁴N)?

solution.explanation: 80 minutes = 4 generations, so one ¹⁵N molecule becomes 2⁴ = 16 molecules. The two original heavy strands are never lost; each ends up in one hybrid molecule. So 2 of 16 molecules (1/8) are hybrid and the remaining 14 (7/8) are light.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1/4 hybrid is the result after 60 minutes (3 generations); 1/2 after 40 minutes (2 generations); 1/16 counts only one hybrid molecule instead of two.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication: the experimental proof
solution.final_answer: Option A: 1/8 hybrid and 7/8 light

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Human genome project and DNA fingerprinting
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements related to the methods and findings of the Human Genome Project are correct?

(a) Sequence annotation is the approach of sequencing the whole genome, coding and non-coding, and later assigning functions to different regions of the sequence.
(b) The genome sequences of several non-human model organisms, such as bacteria, yeast, Caenorhabditis elegans, Drosophila, rice and Arabidopsis, have also been determined.
(c) Repetitive sequences are thought to have no direct coding functions, but they shed light on chromosome structure, dynamics and evolution.
(d) Repetitive sequences make up less than 2 per cent of the human genome and code for most proteins.
(e) The commonly used hosts for cloning DNA fragments in the project were mammalian cells.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Methodologies and findings of the HGP
solution.explanation: Sequence annotation sequences the whole genome and later assigns functions; ESTs instead identify expressed genes. Genomes of model organisms such as bacteria, yeast, C. elegans, Drosophila, rice and Arabidopsis have also been sequenced. Repetitive sequences, repeated hundreds to thousands of times, make up a large portion of the genome, have no direct coding function, but shed light on chromosome structure, dynamics and evolution. DNA fragments were cloned in bacteria and yeast using BAC and YAC vectors.
steps: (d): false, repeats are a large, non-coding part
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and C include (d) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', human genome project: methodologies; salient features
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A mutant E. coli has an altered i gene whose product (the repressor) can no longer bind to the operator. What happens to the structural genes of the lac operon in this mutant when lactose is absent?

options.text: The z, y and a genes stay switched off until lactose is supplied
The z, y and a genes are transcribed even though lactose is absent
Only the i gene is transcribed; the structural genes stay silent
The structural genes are transcribed but cannot be translated in the absence of lactose

solution.concept: Negative regulation of the lac operon
solution.explanation: Normally, in the absence of an inducer, the repressor binds the operator and prevents RNA polymerase from transcribing the operon. If the repressor cannot bind the operator, nothing blocks RNA polymerase, so the structural genes z, y and a are transcribed all the time, whether or not lactose is present.
steps: Operon is switched off only by repressor bound to operator
No binding → no block → continuous transcription
solution.why_others_wrong: Lactose acts only by inactivating the repressor, and here the repressor is already unable to act. The mRNA of the operon needs no lactose to be translated.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', regulation of gene expression: the lac operon
solution.final_answer: Option B: The z, y and a genes are transcribed even though lactose is absent

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The length of the DNA double helix in a typical mammalian cell is about 2.2 metres, far greater than the dimension of a typical nucleus (about 10⁻⁶ m).
Statement II: In eukaryotes, chromatin fibres are further coiled and condensed at the metaphase stage of cell division to form chromosomes.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT multiplies 6.6 × 10⁹ bp by 0.34 × 10⁻⁹ m per bp to get about 2.2 m of DNA, which must fit into a nucleus of about 10⁻⁶ m; hence the need for packaging. Nucleosomes form the chromatin fibre, which is further coiled and condensed at the metaphase stage of cell division to form chromosomes. Both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', packaging of DNA helix
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The genetic code is nearly universal; for example, from bacteria to humans UUU codes for phenylalanine.
Reason (R): AUG has dual functions: it codes for methionine and also acts as the initiator codon.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Universality of the code and the initiator codon
solution.explanation: Both statements are features of the genetic code listed by NCERT. The near-universality of the code (with some exceptions in mitochondrial codons and some protozoans) is a separate feature from the dual role of AUG. R does not explain why UUU means phenylalanine in all these organisms.
steps: Different features of the code → R does not explain A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', genetic code
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If one strand of a DNA segment reads 5'-ATGC-3', its complementary strand, also written in the 5'→3' direction, reads 5'-GCAT-3'.
Reason (R): In double-stranded DNA, the two polynucleotide chains run in the same direction (parallel polarity).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Base pairing gives the complement 3'-TACG-5' opposite 5'-ATGC-3'. Written 5'→3', this is 5'-GCAT-3', so A is true. This works only because the two chains have antiparallel polarity (one 5'→3', the other 3'→5'); R says they are parallel and is false.
steps: R: false, the chains are antiparallel
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', structure of polynucleotide chain: double helix
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a biogas plant, the biogas produced from a slurry of cattle dung is supplied through an outlet pipe to nearby houses. NCERT states that it is used for:

solution.explanation: A biogas plant has a concrete tank in which bio-wastes are collected and a slurry of dung is fed; a floating cover rises as microbial activity produces gas. An outlet pipe carries the gas to nearby houses, where the biogas is used for cooking and lighting.
solution.why_others_wrong: Statins come from the fungus Monascus purpureus, fruit juices are clarified with pectinases and proteases, and Swiss cheese is ripened by Propionibacterium sharmanii; none uses biogas.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in production of biogas
solution.final_answer: Option C: Cooking and lighting

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The ladybird beetle (with red and black markings) and dragonflies are useful biocontrol agents. They help to get rid of, respectively:

solution.explanation: NCERT gives the Ladybird beetle and dragonflies as familiar examples of biological control: the Ladybird is useful to get rid of aphids and dragonflies to get rid of mosquitoes.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option B reverses the pair. Butterfly caterpillars are controlled by Bacillus thuringiensis, and fungal pathogens by Trichoderma.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes as biocontrol agents
solution.final_answer: Option A: Aphids and mosquitoes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, the main sources of biofertilisers are:

solution.explanation: Biofertilisers are organisms that enrich the nutrient quality of the soil. The main sources are bacteria (e.g. Rhizobium, Azotobacter, Azospirillum), fungi (mycorrhiza-forming Glomus) and cyanobacteria (Anabaena, Nostoc, Oscillatoria).
solution.why_others_wrong: Urea and phosphate salts are chemical fertilisers; insects, nematodes, viruses and protozoa are not the sources NCERT lists.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes as biofertilisers
solution.final_answer: Option D: Bacteria, fungi and cyanobacteria

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In paddy fields, cyanobacteria are weeds that reduce soil fertility.
Statement II: Plants having mycorrhizal associations show resistance to root-borne pathogens, tolerance to salinity and drought, and an overall increase in plant growth and development.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Cyanobacteria are autotrophic microbes, many of which fix atmospheric nitrogen; in paddy fields they serve as an important biofertiliser and also add organic matter, increasing fertility. Statement I is false. Besides helping in phosphorus absorption, mycorrhiza (e.g. Glomus) gives the plant resistance to root-borne pathogens, tolerance to salinity and drought and better overall growth. Statement II is true.
steps: Statement I: false, cyanobacteria are an important biofertiliser in paddy
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes as biofertilisers
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In secondary treatment, the primary effluent is passed into large aeration tanks where it is constantly agitated mechanically and air is pumped into it.
Reason (R): Agitation and aeration promote the growth of anaerobic methanogens, which form flocs in the aeration tank.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: A is NCERT's description of the aeration tank. The purpose is to allow vigorous growth of useful aerobic microbes into flocs (bacteria associated with fungal filaments), which consume the organic matter and reduce the BOD. Methanogens are anaerobic and act later, in the anaerobic sludge digesters. R is false.
steps: R: false, aeration favours aerobic flocs; methanogens work in anaerobic digesters

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A population of 250 individuals grows exponentially according to Nₜ = N₀e^(rt), with r = 0.0231 per year. Taking ln 2 = 0.693, what will the population size be after 60 years?

solution.explanation: rt = 0.0231 × 60 = 1.386 = 2 × 0.693 = 2 ln 2. So e^(rt) = e^(2 ln 2) = 2² = 4, and Nₜ = 250 × 4 = 1000. The population doubles every 0.693/0.0231 = 30 years, i.e. twice in 60 years.
solution.shortcut: Doubling time = ln 2 / r = 30 years; 60 years = 2 doublings.
solution.why_others_wrong: 500 counts only one doubling; 597 treats growth as linear, 250 × (1 + rt); 2000 counts three doublings.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population growth: exponential growth

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A field receives 10,00,000 kJ of incident solar radiation. solution.concept: From incident radiation to net primary productivity

solution.explanation: Decomposition is quicker when detritus is rich in nitrogen and water-soluble substances such as sugars, and slower when it is rich in lignin and chitin. A warm and moist environment favours decomposition, while low temperature and anaerobiosis inhibit it; decomposition is largely an oxygen-requiring process. Both favourable factors occur together only in the keyed option.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A has resistant lignin; option C has good chemistry but cold, anaerobic conditions; option D has both resistant chitin and cold, dry conditions.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', decomposition
solution.final_answer: Option B: Nitrogen-rich leaf litter with plenty of soluble sugars, in warm, moist, well-aerated soil

questions.question_text: For islands within one region, the species–area relationship follows log S = log C + Z log A with Z = 0.2. If island Q is 32 times larger in area than island P, how many times more species is island Q expected to have?

solution.explanation: log S = log C + Z log A means S = C·A^Z. So S_Q/S_P = (A_Q/A_P)^Z = 32^0.2. Since 32 = 2⁵, 32^0.2 = 2^(5 × 0.2) = 2¹ = 2.

solution.final_answer: Option C: 2 times
